spatial_claims.claim: Points A, C, D, B are collinear on line AB, with C bisecting AB and D cutting AB unequally
AC = CB (C is the midpoint of AB)
D lies on segment CB, giving collinear order A-C-D-B, so AD = AC + CD
Line AD is cut at C into segments AC and CD (C between A and D)
Line CB is cut at D into segments CD and DB (D between C and B)

configuration_map: Four collinear points on a straight line in order A-C-D-B. C is the midpoint of AB (AC = CB). D is between C and B, creating the unequal cut. No auxiliary points, no angles, no triangles or circles are constructed. The entire proof operates algebraically on segments of this single line, applying Props 2.4 and 2.7 as algebraic identities and then performing arithmetic substitution and cancellation.

The only spatial claims concern collinear point ordering (betweenness), which are trivially consistent. No angle decompositions, no interior/exterior arguments, no auxiliary geometric constructions that could create configuration contradictions. All algebraic steps (addition, substitution via AC=CB, cancellation) are valid.
